Note: it is now one of the largest Catholic pilgrimage sites in the world.
205: Which Christian prayer sums up the faith and begins “I believe in God”?
Note: its name comes from the Latin “credo”, meaning “I believe”.
206: What colour vestments do Catholic priests wear at Pentecost?
Note: red recalls the tongues of fire and is also used for the feasts of martyrs.
207: What is the Sunday after Easter traditionally called, after the first Latin words of its Mass?
Note: Victor Hugo gave this name to his bell-ringer, who was found on that day.
208: Which Catholic prayer is traditionally said morning, noon and evening at the sound of the bells?
Note: the painter Millet depicted it in a famous painting from 1859.
209: According to the Gospel of Luke, which song of Mary begins “My soul proclaims the greatness of the Lord”?
Note: it is sung every evening at Vespers.
210: What are the monster sculptures that drain rainwater from cathedrals called?
Note: the water comes out of their mouths, away from the walls, to protect them.
211: The famous leaning tower of which Italian city is the bell tower of its cathedral?
Note: it began to lean while it was still being built, because the ground was too soft.
212: What is the circle of light painted around the heads of saints called?
Note: in Christian art, it shows that a figure is holy.
213: What are the pictures made of small pieces of stone or glass that decorate Byzantine churches called?
Note: those in Ravenna, Italy, are among the most famous.
214: What is a religious man who lives alone, far from the world, to pray called?
Note: the first Christian hermits lived in the Egyptian desert.
215: According to legend, which saint, patron of travellers, carried the Child Jesus across a river?
Note: his name means “Christ-bearer” in Greek.
216: In which city is the Cathedral of St. Michael and St. Gudula?
Note: Saint Gudula is one of the city's patron saints.
217: In which German city does a huge Gothic cathedral, completed in 1880, stand on the banks of the Rhine?
Note: its construction, begun in 1248, took more than 6 centuries.
218: What is the covered walkway around a garden at the heart of a monastery called?
Note: monks walked there while meditating or reading.
219: In which Italian city does a basilica keep, according to tradition, the relics of Mark the Evangelist?
Note: the winged lion, symbol of Saint Mark, became the city's emblem.
220: Which Italian saint founded the monastery of Monte Cassino and wrote a rule for monks?
Note: his rule, written in the 6th century, is still followed by many monks today.
221: Which 4th-century Egyptian saint, celebrated on 17 January, is often shown with a pig?
Note: he is regarded as the father of Christian monasticism.
222: What is the order of “preaching friars”, approved by the Pope in 1216, called?
Note: the order was founded by a Spanish priest, Dominic de Guzmán.
223: Which English monk, known as “the Venerable”, wrote a history of the Church in England around 731?
Note: he helped popularise counting years from the birth of Christ.
224: Which 6th-century Irish monk founded the monastery on the island of Iona, in Scotland?
Note: from Iona, his monks spread Christianity across the north of Britain.
